svg.text: Sources of Public International Law (Article 38(1) ICJ Statute)
Statute of the International Court of Justice · Primary Sources vs Subsidiary Means
Expressly recognized rules by contesting states · Bilateral & Multilateral · Pacta Sunt Servanda (Art. 26 VCLT 1969) · Jus Cogens (Art. 53 VCLT)
Evidence of a general practice accepted as law · Two Essential Elements: (1) State Practice (Diuturnitas) + (2) Opinio Juris Sive Necessitatis (North Sea Continental Shelf Case)
Article 38(1)(c): General Principles of Law Recognized by Civilized Nations (Primary)
Fundamental legal maxims: Res Judicata, Estoppel, Good Faith (Bona Fides), Subrogation, Reparation for Breach (Chorzow Factory Case 1928)
Article 38(1)(d): Judicial Decisions & Scholarly Teachings (Subsidiary Means)
Judgments of ICJ (subject to Art. 59: No formal stare decisis) · Municipal High Court decisions · Teachings of highly qualified publicists (Grotius, Oppenheim)
Article 38(2) Special Prerogative: The Court may decide a case ex aequo et bono (justice and fairness outside strict law) ONLY IF the parties agree thereto.
